The structure is described in a cubic setting with the space-group symmetry I-43d, number 220, whose Hall symbol is "I -4bd 2c 3". The supplied input cell is not the conventional cubic cell but a rhombohedrally distorted primitive one: all three input lattice vectors have the same length, 7.26400978 Å, and each pair of input axes meets at an angle of 109.47122063°, the tetrahedral angle characteristic of a body-centered cubic lattice expressed in primitive rhombohedral axes. This input cell contains eight sodium atoms, corresponding to the declared composition Na₈.

All atomic positions are given as fractional coordinates. The standard crystallographic frame and the input frame are related by q_standard = P q_input + s, where the matrix P has rows (0.5, −0.5, 0.5), (0.5, 0.5, −0.5), and (−0.5, 0.5, 0.5), and the origin shift s is (−2.5254088791396506×10⁻¹⁷, 0, 0), effectively zero within numerical precision. This transformation converts coordinates from the primitive rhombohedral input cell into the conventional body-centered cubic setting of space group I-43d.

In the standard frame, the sodium atoms occupy a single independent crystallographic orbit, the Wyckoff position 16c, with multiplicity 16 in the conventional body-centered cell. The representative atom of this orbit lies at fractional coordinates (x, x, x) with x = 0.02650800000000009, so the representative position is approximately (0.026508, 0.026508, 0.026508) when rounded to six digits. Because this is the only independent orbit, the entire structure consists of symmetry-equivalent sodium atoms generated from this one threefold-axis position by the operations of I-43d together with the body-centering translation. The eight atoms in the primitive input cell correspond to half of the sixteen atoms in the conventional body-centered cell, consistent with the primitive-to-conventional relationship.

No precision corrections are required beyond the stated rounding to six digits; the listed representative coordinate already defines the input geometry.
